tagline.text: Sunset soaks in a mangrove cove at the Philippines' only saltwater hot spring

location.label: Location
location.text: Maquinit area, Barangay Tagumpay, Coron, Palawan, on the coast east of Coron town

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱600~1,100 (entrance fee and tricycle round trip, for 1–2 people)

children.text: Maquinit Hot Spring is a geothermal saltwater spring on a mangrove-lined shore, a 20–30 minute tricycle ride from Coron town. It is popular as an evening plan: soak in warm water of 38–40 degrees and watch the sun set over Coron Bay.

Maquinit Hot Spring sits in the Maquinit area of Barangay Tagumpay, east of Coron town, on the southern coast of Busuanga Island in northern Palawan. A mangrove forest surrounds the narrow strip of shore between the mountain and the sea, and seawater heated by underground geothermal activity flows into the pools. For that reason, many travel guides describe it as the only saltwater hot spring in the Philippines. Unlike ordinary hot springs, the water is salty and slightly sticky, so you float easily, and it is said to be good for the skin and muscles. Treat those benefits as local belief rather than scientifically confirmed fact.
The facilities are simple. The main pool has a pebble floor and holds up to about
100 people
, and guides mention two smaller pools plus a separate shallow pool for children. Wooden decks connect the pools and look out over the limestone islands across Coron Bay. The water is usually
, and near the vents it reportedly reaches about
. Soaking in the heat of the day can make you dizzy, so most visitors come as the sun goes down. The routine is to cool off in the misting area beside the deck and then get back in, again and again.

It pairs well with a Coron town tour, so it is often added to a half-day itinerary together with the Mount Tapyas viewpoint and St. Augustine Church. It is also a good way to ease tired muscles after a full day of island hopping by boat. Know in advance, though, that because the water is saltwater the only showers are the misting area, and that the last stretch of road is rough. The prices and hours in this guide were compared across several guides and operating details published in 2026 and may change with local conditions, so check the latest announcements before you go.

Coron is famous for island-hopping highlights such as Kayangan Lake, Barracuda Lake, and Twin Lagoon, but this is a land attraction that needs no boat and takes little time, so it also works as a rainy-day alternative. Many travelers visit just the hot spring on days when island hopping is canceled because of rough seas. Visitor numbers are not large on an average day, but between about 5 PM and 7 PM tour groups arrive all at once and it gets crowded, so the time you choose greatly affects how much you enjoy it.

blocks.title: The Philippines' only saltwater hot spring

children.text: The pools are fed by seawater heated by geothermal activity, so the water tastes salty and your body floats lightly. It feels different from an ordinary freshwater hot spring and is counted as an experience you can have only in Coron. The water is not for drinking, so be careful not to swallow it.

The wooden decks linking the pools run over mangrove roots. Around sunset the glow spreads over the limestone islands and the bay, which makes for great photos, and early in the morning monitor lizards are sometimes seen in the mangroves. Do not feed or touch the animals.
The pebble-floored large pool holds about
100 people
, and the two small pools are said to be hotter. It is safer to let your body adjust in the large pool first and then move to the hotter small pools.

This spot beside the deck is where you cool off between soaks. Getting out of the spring, cooling down here, and going back in again and again helps reduce dizziness. Guides say there are no freshwater showers, so bring a change of clothes and a towel.
Around dusk the air is cool and the heat of the water feels even better, making this the most popular time. You must be out before closing time in the evening at
, so it is best to arrive before sunset, watch the sky first, and then soak.

blocks.title: The finishing stop of a Coron town tour

children.text: It is often the last stop on a town tour that covers the Mount Tapyas viewpoint, St. Augustine Church, Lualhati Park, and a cashew factory. Some tour packages include the entrance fee, so it helps to check when you book.

A separate children's pool is provided, so guides describe it as a good place to bring kids. The floor is slippery pebbles, however, adult supervision is needed, and young children should not stay long in the high temperature.

items.title: Coron town half-day course
items.subtitle: From the viewpoint to a hot spring sunset

children.text: Set out from your hotel in Coron town and climb to the Mount Tapyas viewpoint to see the town and the bay. The path is a staircase, so the afternoon is better than the heat of midday.
Come back down to town and take a light look around nearby spots such as St. Augustine Church or Lualhati Park.
Ride a tricycle toward Maquinit Hot Spring. The last stretch of road is rough, so the ride is slow.
Arrive and pay the entrance fee, then walk the decks to find the pools and the misting area. Ease into the large pool slowly while watching the sunset.
Repeat soaks of around 10 minutes with rests in between, and drink plenty of water.
This is the last entry time, so wrap up, leave, and ride a tricycle back to town for dinner.
Tour groups crowd in after 5 PM, so if you want a quiet visit, arrive earlier or consider a weekday morning.

items.title: Post-hopping relaxation course
items.subtitle: Island tour in the morning, hot spring in the evening

children.text: Start an island-hopping tour that includes Kayangan Lake, Twin Lagoon, and other stops.
Finish the tour, shower at your hotel, and have a light snack.
Take a tricycle to the hot spring and go in around sunset.
Wash up and change, then return to town for dinner.
On days when island hopping has left you tired, keep the soak short and rehydrate well.
Direct flights run from Manila Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) to Busuanga Airport (USU, near Coron), and the flight takes about
1 hour 10 minutes
. Airlines and schedules change by season, so check when you book.
From Busuanga Airport to Coron town you travel by van or taxi; check the fare and travel time locally.
You can also reach Coron from Puerto Princesa by boat or van, but it takes a long time, so most people fly.
A tricycle from Coron town is the most common way. The distance varies by guide at about
5–8 km
, and the ride takes about
20–30 minutes
. You often bargain for a round trip of
with the driver waiting at the entrance.
Some write-ups say the fare goes up if the wait runs long, so agree on the waiting time and the total before you set off.
The last
is unpaved, so it turns muddy in wet weather and the ride is slow.
Guides say that a Coron town tour can combine Maquinit with Mount Tapyas, a church, and a cashew factory for about
per person. Whether the entrance fee is included depends on the package.
You can also rent a scooter, but the last stretch of road is rough and has no streetlights, so the ride back after dark is dangerous. It is not recommended for beginners.

The hot spring is open all year, but in the November–May dry season the road is dry and the sky is clear, which makes for good sunsets. The air is especially cool from December–February, so the hot water feels even more comfortable. In the June–October rainy season the road gets slippery and muddy, and more people come instead on days when island hopping is canceled because of rough seas.

During the day, arriving between about 4:30 PM and 5 PM as the sun sinks is the popular choice. From 5 to 7 PM is the busiest time, when town tour groups crowd in, and for a quiet visit a weekday morning between 8 and 9 AM is better.

The only food at the hot spring is a kiosk selling a few drinks and snacks, so most people eat in Coron town. Because it closes early, the easiest approach is to stay in town and go in the evening. If you pick a place to stay near the center of Coron town, tricycle rides are easy and the island-hopping docks are close too.

Have dinner at a seafood restaurant or Filipino restaurant in town, and avoid heavy meals and alcohol before soaking. It is good to drink plenty of water before and after soaking. Specific hotels and restaurants in Coron change with the season, so check recent reviews before you decide.
Many guides say the entrance fee is accepted in cash only, so bring ₱500–1,000 bills and small change.
Stay in the water only about 10 minutes at a time and take breaks in between. Lower yourself in slowly.
The pebble floor is slippery and rough, so wear water shoes or sandals with good grip.
Bring a towel, a change of clothes, and water. Guides say the only shower is the misting area, and there are no lockers or towel rental.
Drink about 500 ml of water before soaking and another 500 ml while you soak to prevent dehydration.
The water is salty and cannot be drunk. It may sting if it gets in your eyes or on a wound.
The road is dark after sunset, so agree on a pick-up time with your tricycle driver.
Avoiding 5–7 PM, when tour groups crowd in, lets you enjoy it more quietly.
Keep valuables on you or leave them at your hotel.
If you have high blood pressure or a heart condition, are pregnant, or are taking medication, talk to a doctor before soaking. If you feel dizzy, get out at once and rest in the misting area.
Avoid soaking after drinking alcohol, as it is dangerous. Do not go in alone, and children and non-swimmers need an adult beside them.
If you feel chest pain, dizziness, an irregular heartbeat, difficulty breathing, or nausea, get out immediately and seek medical help if necessary.
The last unpaved stretch has no streetlights and a rough surface. Riding a scooter after dark is dangerous.

The water is hot and the floor is slippery, so keep your phone and camera away from water.
The town the hot spring belongs to; in
Coron
you can find lodging, restaurants, and island-hopping tours, and you get around by tricycle.
A signature Coron island-hopping stop,
Kayangan Lake
is known for its clear limestone lake and viewpoint, and it can be combined with the hot spring on the same day.
Two lagoons where seawater comes and goes,
Twin Lagoon (Coron)
is a popular hopping stop, and the hot spring suits a rest after hopping.
A mysterious lake with temperature layers,
Barracuda Lake
is known for snorkeling and fits into a Coron itinerary.
A viewpoint behind Coron town where you climb stairs to see the town and the bay, and it is often included in the same town tour as the hot spring.
